messages.author: 596f056d3717fc05
messages.subject: checkOriginalDateTime preventing recordTable from working
parts:
Dear camtrapR community,

When I run recordTable on a folder of photos,  the following fatal error pops up everytime it reaches this station subfolder ("ML 13"):

Error in if (any(intable$DateTimeOriginal == "-")) { :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I tested the remaining individual subfolders and confirmed that the problem came from this single station. I then went to the source code and found that it was most likely in checkDateTimeOriginal (https://rdrr.io/cran/camtrapR/src/R/variousOtherHelperFunctions.R).

I tried using the code line that caused the error (any(intable$DateTimeOriginal == "-")) with a subset of the metadata table (ML13 as attached) but simply got FALSE (which is contrary to what the error says).

any(ML13$DateTimeOriginal == "-")
> FALSE

I'm at a loss as to what to do next. Any tip/guidance would be helpful. I'm using camtrapR v2.2.0 and updated both R/RStudio last week.

Thanks a lot!
Phuong

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: checkOriginalDateTime preventing recordTable from working
parts:
Hi, 
this may be due to a problem with daylight saving time. Some of your records were on 2020-03-29, which was the beginning of DST in many countries. If your records happens to fall between 2 and 3 am that day, that time cannot exist, DateTimeOriginal becomes NA, and the function may fail. 
Now the records you shared are not between 2 and 3am, but maybe the timeZone argument somehow pushes them to that hour. How did you specify timeZone?
Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: checkOriginalDateTime preventing recordTable from working
parts:
The issue was caused by corrupted metadata in the images which garbled the DateTimeOriginal and made it unreadable (which caused an unexpected NA in DateTimeOriginal where the function expected "-" or a date-time). It had nothing to do with time zones or DST.

A recent commit to the GitHub version fixed the error by sow skipping these images with a warning.
